item.title: AC
item.dc:creator: ciwg_CEO@906
item.content:encoded: AC, A.C. or Ac may refer to: Air conditioning, technologies for altering the temperature and humidity of air; Alternating current, a type of electrical current in which the current repeatedly changes direction.

item.title: ACCA
item.dc:creator: ciwg_CEO@906
item.content:encoded: Air-Conditioning Contractors of America.

item.title: Acoustical
item.dc:creator: ciwg_CEO@906
item.content:encoded: Of or pertaining to sound.

item.title: AC or DC
item.dc:creator: ciwg_CEO@906
item.content:encoded: Abbreviation for equipment capable of operating on alternating or direct current.

item.title: A-Coil
item.dc:creator: ciwg_CEO@906
item.content:encoded: A heat exchanger (evaporator coil) consisting of two diagonal coils that are joined together in a manner that looks like the letter "A".

item.title: AFUE
item.dc:creator: ciwg_CEO@906
item.content:encoded: Annual Fuel Utilization Efficiency. A measure of a gas furnace's efficiency in converting fuel to energy—the higher the rating, the more efficient the unit.

item.title: AGA
item.dc:creator: ciwg_CEO@906
item.content:encoded: Abbreviation for American Gas Association, Inc.

item.title: Air Conditioner
item.dc:creator: ciwg_CEO@906
item.content:encoded: Any device that can change the temperature, humidity or general quality of the air. More specifically, an air conditioner makes your home cooler, by drawing heat energy out of the house and transferring that heat to the outdoors

item.title: Air cleaner (also Air Filtration System)
item.dc:creator: ciwg_CEO@906
item.content:encoded: Removes airborne allergens from your home.

item.title: Air Filtration System (also Air Cleaner)
item.dc:creator: ciwg_CEO@906
item.content:encoded: Removes airborne allergens from your home.

item.title: Air flow volume
item.dc:creator: ciwg_CEO@906
item.content:encoded: The amount of air the system circulates through your home, expressed in cubic feet per minute (cfm). Proper air flow depends on the outdoor unit, the indoor unit, the ductwork and even whether the filters are clean.

item.title: Air handler
item.dc:creator: ciwg_CEO@906
item.content:encoded: An air moving and/or mixing unit. Residential air handlers include a blower, a coil, an expansion device, a heater rack and a filter. Heaters for air handlers are sold as accessories. In some models, heaters are factory installed. The portion of your heating and cooling system that forces air through your home’s ductwork.

item.title: AHRI
item.dc:creator: ciwg_CEO@906
item.content:encoded: Air Conditioning, Heating & Refrigeration Institute

item.title: ASHRAE
item.dc:creator: ciwg_CEO@906
item.content:encoded:
American Society of Heating, Refrigeration and Air Conditioning Engineers- ASHRAE is an international voluntary organization for people involved in heating, ventilation, air conditioning, or refrigeration (HVAC&R).
The society promotes the general sciences of HVAC&R. The main Society headquarters is located in Atlanta, Georgia with local chapters located across the United States and throughout the world.
ASHRAE publishes a four-volume Handbook that serves as a resource for members, with one of the four volumes updated each year. ASHRAE also publishes a well recognized series of standards and guidelines relating to HVAC Systems. ASHRAE Standards are often referenced in other model building codes and in the US Green Building Council’s Leadership in Energy Design (LEED) green building rating system.

item.title: BTU
item.dc:creator: ciwg_CEO@906
item.content:encoded: British thermal unit; the amount of heat required to raise or lower the temperature of one pound of water one degree Fahrenheit. The heat extracted from your home by an air conditioner is measured in BTUs.

item.title: BTUH
item.dc:creator: ciwg_CEO@906
item.content:encoded: British thermal units per hour. 12,000 BTUH equals one ton of cooling.

item.title: Burner
item.dc:creator: ciwg_CEO@906
item.content:encoded: A device that uses fuel to support combustion.

item.title: Burner Orifice
item.dc:creator: ciwg_CEO@906
item.content:encoded: The opening through which gas flows to the air/gas mixing chamber of the burner.

item.title: Burner (sealed combustion)
item.dc:creator: ciwg_CEO@906
item.content:encoded: A burner that obtains all air for combustion from outside the heated space.

item.title: CADR Clean Air Delivery Rate (CADR)
item.dc:creator: ciwg_CEO@906
item.content:encoded: Provides the number of cubic feet of clean air that a unit delivers each minute. Efficiency of the system times the airflow of the system.
